text.p: Two large earthquakes in China's northwestern Xinjiang region, which struck within hours of each other, have injured 17 people and destroyed or damaged thousands of buildings, officials said on Monday.
No deaths had been reported from the two earthquakes measuring 6.3 and 6.4 on the open-ended Richter scale that struck the town of Jiashi on Sunday, officials said.
However, at least 17 people were injured, including six who were in serious condition, an official of the Jiashi Seismological Bureau said by telephone.
At least 3,000 buildings, mainly earthen homes, were destroyed or damaged by Sunday's tremors, he said.
The number of casualties was limited because most residents of Jiashi had been living in tents since January when an earthquake of magnitude 6.4 rocked the district, killing about 50 people, he said.
"There are almost no buildings now in Jiashi that have not been damaged," the official said. "Everyone lives and eats and sleeps outside in tents."

More than 4,000 earthquakes and aftershocks have jolted the region that is populated mainly by cotton farmers and sheep herders since January, and seismologists have warned of more tremors in the region.
"It feels as if the ground never stops shaking," the official said.
On March 20, an earthquake measuring 6.9 hit Jiashi, killing 24 people and injuring 40. That came just days after a tremor of 6.0 magnitude left two people dead and injured three.
